name: Two-dimensional plasmons in graphene and 2DEGs
summary: Electrons in graphene and semiconductor 2DEGs support gate-tunable 2D plasmons with omega~sqrt(q), imaged by infrared nano-imaging; drift-driven plasma-wave instabilities in field-effect transistors (Dyakonov-Shur) are the solid-state analogue of streaming instabilities and are used for THz detection.
sources: Chen et al. (2012). "Optical nano-imaging of gate-tunable graphene plasmons". *Nature* 487, 77. [doi:10.1038/nature11254](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature11254)

Dyakonov & Shur (1993). "Shallow water analogy for a ballistic field effect transistor: New mechanism of plasma wave generation by dc current". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 2465. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.71.2465](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.71.2465)

name: Exciton Mott transition by plasma screening
summary: At high photoexcitation density, screening by free carriers in 2D semiconductors shortens the screening length below the exciton radius, so excitons ionize into an electron-hole plasma with giant band-gap renormalization; this is the Mott criterion for pressure ionization in dense plasmas.
sources: Chernikov et al. (2015). "Population inversion and giant bandgap renormalization in atomically thin WS2 layers". *Nat. Photonics* 9, 466. [doi:10.1038/nphoton.2015.104](https://doi.org/10.1038/nphoton.2015.104)

name: Non-reciprocal forces in complex plasmas and active matter
summary: Ion wakes downstream of levitated dust grains make grain-grain forces non-reciprocal, violating Newton's third law and breaking detailed balance; complex plasmas thus become a model system for the non-reciprocal and odd interactions central to active matter.
map: \mathbf F_{ij}\neq-\mathbf F_{ji}\Rightarrow\text{no Boltzmann distribution};\ T_i\neq T_j\ \text{for distinct species}
sources: Ivlev et al. (2015). "Statistical Mechanics where Newton's Third Law is Broken". *Phys. Rev. X* 5, 011035. [arXiv:1411.3982](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.3982)

name: Yukawa plasma crystals and colloidal crystals
summary: Charged dust grains in a plasma and charged colloids in an electrolyte both interact by a screened-Coulomb (Yukawa/DLVO) potential, crystallize when the coupling parameter is large, and let melting, defects and phonons be watched particle by particle.
breaks: Dusty plasmas are underdamped, strongly driven and open (charging currents, ion wakes), while colloids are overdamped by the solvent and in thermal equilibrium.
sources: Thomas et al. (1994). "Plasma Crystal: Coulomb Crystallization in a Dusty Plasma". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 73, 652. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.652](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.652)

name: Quantum Monte Carlo for the warm dense electron gas
summary: Quantum Monte Carlo for the uniform electron gas, which underpins LDA exchange-correlation in condensed matter, was extended to finite temperature (path-integral and configuration PIMC) to give the warm-dense-matter exchange-correlation free energy, fighting the same fermion sign problem.
sources: Ceperley & Alder (1980). "Ground State of the Electron Gas by a Stochastic Method". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 45, 566. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.45.566](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.45.566)
Dornheim, Groth & Bonitz (2018). "The uniform electron gas at warm dense matter conditions". *Phys. Rep.* 744, 1. [arXiv:1801.05783](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.05783)

name: Nb3Sn and NbTi magnets for tokamaks
summary: The toroidal and poloidal field coils of ITER, JT-60SA, EAST and KSTAR are low-temperature type-II superconductors (Nb3Sn, NbTi) whose upper critical field, flux pinning and strain sensitivity set the achievable field and hence confinement.

name: Frozen-in flux vs Meissner flux expulsion
summary: An ideal-MHD plasma is a perfect conductor in which magnetic flux is frozen into the fluid, whereas a superconductor is more than a perfect conductor: London's equation actively expels flux; the contrast is the standard way to show the Meissner effect is thermodynamic, not just zero resistance.
map: \partial_t\mathbf B=\nabla\times(\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)\ (\eta\to0,\ \dot{\mathbf B}=0\text{ in a static perfect conductor})\ \text{vs}\ \nabla\times\mathbf J_s=-\frac{n_se^2}{m}\mathbf B\Rightarrow\mathbf B=0
breaks: Ideal MHD has no condensate or gap and keeps whatever flux it started with; a superconductor reaches a unique equilibrium with B=0 inside, set by a macroscopic phase.

name: Photon mass: plasma cutoff and Meissner effect
summary: Transverse light in a plasma obeys omega^2=omega_p^2+c^2k^2, as if photons had mass hbar*omega_p/c^2; Anderson used this plasma analogy to show that in a superconductor the Goldstone mode is absorbed and the photon becomes massive, giving London penetration depth lambda_L=c/omega_p(n_s), the step that became the Higgs mechanism.
sources: Anderson (1963). "Plasmons, Gauge Invariance, and Mass". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 439. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.439](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.439)

name: REBCO high-temperature superconductors for compact tokamaks
summary: Rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO) cuprate tapes carry high currents at 20 K and above 20 T, allowing compact high-field tokamaks (SPARC, ARC) because fusion power density scales as B^4 at fixed beta; quench protection and neutron degradation of the cuprate are open engineering problems.
sources: Creely et al. (2020). "Overview of the SPARC tokamak". *J. Plasma Phys.* 86, 865860502. [doi:10.1017/S0022377820001257](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0022377820001257)

name: Dense hydrogen: superconductors and laser-shock experiments
summary: The insulator-metal transition of dense hydrogen and deuterium, the root of the metallic-hydrogen and hydride-superconductor programme, is probed both in diamond-anvil cells and in dynamic compression at NIF and the Z machine; the two disagree on the transition pressure, partly because of temperature and DFT functional choices.
sources: Knudson et al. (2015). "Direct observation of an abrupt insulator-to-metal transition in dense liquid deuterium". *Science* 348, 1455. [doi:10.1126/science.aaa7471](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaa7471)
Celliers et al. (2018). "Insulator-metal transition in dense fluid deuterium". *Science* 361, 677. [doi:10.1126/science.aat0970](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0970)

name: Band topology of magnetized plasma waves
summary: Chern numbers and bulk-boundary correspondence, developed for electronic bands, classify the wave bands of magnetized cold plasmas; a topological gaseous plasmon polariton is predicted at plasma interfaces with a sign change of B or density.
map: C_n=\frac1{2\pi}\int\Omega_n(\mathbf k)d^2k\ \text{for the Maxwell-fluid eigenproblem }\omega\psi=H(\mathbf k)\psi
sources: Parker et al. (2020). "Topological Gaseous Plasmon Polariton in Realistic Plasma". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 124, 195001. [arXiv:1911.02148](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.02148)

name: Guiding-centre drift and the Hall effect
summary: In crossed E and B fields charged particles drift at E x B / B^2 regardless of charge or mass; in a 2D electron gas this drift gives the classical Hall conductivity, and quantized cyclotron orbits (Landau levels) with skipping orbits at edges become the chiral edge states of the quantum Hall effect.

name: Band theory behind semiconductor devices
summary: Bloch bands, effective masses, doping and carrier statistics from solid-state theory are the design language of transistors, LEDs and solar cells; device equations (drift-diffusion, Shockley diode, Shockley-Queisser) are band theory plus non-equilibrium carrier kinetics.

name: Tight binding as periodic LCAO / Huckel theory
summary: The tight-binding band model is the molecular-orbital LCAO (Huckel) method applied to a periodic lattice: graphene's pi bands are the infinite-molecule limit of benzene's Huckel orbitals, and Slater-Koster parameters play the role of resonance integrals.
map: E(\mathbf k)=\epsilon_0+\sum_{\mathbf R}t(\mathbf R)e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf R}\leftrightarrow\text{H\"uckel }E=\alpha+2\beta\cos\frac{2\pi j}{N}
sources: Slater & Koster (1954). "Simplified LCAO Method for the Periodic Potential Problem". *Phys. Rev.* 94, 1498. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.94.1498](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.94.1498)

name: STM imaging of the local density of states
summary: STM, developed in surface science, measures the sample's local density of states via tunnelling (Tersoff-Hamann); spectroscopic STM became a core probe of band structure, superconducting gaps, vortex cores and quasiparticle interference in quantum materials.
sources: Binnig et al. (1982). "Surface Studies by Scanning Tunneling Microscopy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 49, 57. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.57](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.57)
Tersoff & Hamann (1985). "Theory of the scanning tunneling microscope". *Phys. Rev. B* 31, 805. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.31.805](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.31.805)

name: Synchrotron and XFEL light for crystallography
summary: Undulator synchrotron and free-electron-laser X-rays provide the brilliance for structure determination, resonant and inelastic scattering, and femtosecond diffraction of solids; Bragg's law and the structure factor are the analysis framework.
sources: Otwinowski & Minor (1997). "Processing of X-ray diffraction data collected in oscillation mode". *Methods Enzymol.* 276, 307. [doi:10.1016/s0076-6879(97)76066-x](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0076-6879(97)76066-x)

name: Superionic conductors for solid-state batteries
summary: Solid electrolytes such as Li10GeP2S12 are superionic crystals in which a rigid anion framework hosts liquid-like Li-ion diffusion through connected sites; crystal structure and its percolating channels set ionic conductivity.
sources: Kamaya et al. (2011). "A lithium superionic conductor". *Nat. Mater.* 10, 682. [doi:10.1038/nmat3066](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmat3066)

name: Surface crystallography and reconstruction
summary: Surfaces have their own 2D lattices and reciprocal lattices; low-energy electron diffraction and STM reveal reconstructions such as Si(111) 7x7, extending bulk diffraction theory to the 17 wallpaper groups.
sources: Binnig et al. (1983). "7 × 7 Reconstruction on Si(111) Resolved in Real Space". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 50, 120. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.120](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.120)

name: Mantle and core mineral phases behind seismic structure
summary: The post-perovskite transition of MgSiO3, found by high-pressure X-ray diffraction and ab initio theory, explains the D'' seismic discontinuity above the core-mantle boundary, and hcp iron's elastic anisotropy explains inner-core seismic anisotropy.
sources: Murakami et al. (2004). "Post-Perovskite Phase Transition in MgSiO3". *Science* 304, 855. [doi:10.1126/science.1095932](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1095932)

Oganov & Ono (2004). "Theoretical and experimental evidence for a post-perovskite phase of MgSiO3 in Earth's D″ layer". *Nature* 430, 445. [doi:10.1038/nature02701](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02701)

name: High-throughput DFT for battery and energy materials
summary: Databases of DFT-computed formation energies, voltages and phase stability (Materials Project and successors), now accelerated by machine-learned potentials, screen cathodes, electrolytes and thermoelectrics before synthesis.
sources: Jain et al. (2013). "Commentary: The Materials Project: A materials genome approach to accelerating materials innovation". *APL Mater.* 1, 011002. [doi:10.1063/1.4812323](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4812323)

name: Chemical physics uses condensed-matter DFT
summary: Chemical physics borrows DFT and periodic electronic-structure methods for spectroscopy, reaction barriers and surface chemistry.

name: DFT shared by solid-state and quantum chemistry
summary: Kohn-Sham DFT is the workhorse of both communities; chemistry contributed hybrid and dispersion-corrected functionals (B3LYP, M06, DFT-D) while physics contributed plane-wave pseudopotential codes, and both test against wavefunction methods such as coupled cluster.
sources: Kohn & Sham (1965). "Self-Consistent Equations Including Exchange and Correlation Effects". *Phys. Rev.* 140, A1133. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.140.A1133](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.140.A1133)
Becke (1993). "Density-functional thermochemistry. III. The role of exact exchange". *J. Chem. Phys.* 98, 5648. [doi:10.1063/1.464913](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.464913)

name: d-band theory and descriptor-based catalyst design
summary: DFT calculations of adsorption energies on metal surfaces, organized by the position of the d-band centre and linear scaling relations, explain why gold is inert and drive computational screening of catalysts through volcano plots.
sources: Hammer & Nørskov (1995). "Why gold is the noblest of all the metals". *Nature* 376, 238. [doi:10.1038/376238a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/376238a0)

Zhao et al. (2019). "Theory-guided design of catalytic materials using scaling relationships and reactivity descriptors". *Nat. Rev. Mater.* 4, 792. [doi:10.1038/s41578-019-0152-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41578-019-0152-x)

name: Ab initio mineral physics of Earth's deep interior
summary: DFT elastic constants and melting curves of iron alloys and silicates at 100-360 GPa supply the seismic velocities, densities and core temperature that seismology alone cannot fix, at conditions difficult to reach in experiments.
sources: Oganov & Ono (2004). "Theoretical and experimental evidence for a post-perovskite phase of MgSiO3 in Earth's D″ layer". *Nature* 430, 445. [doi:10.1038/nature02701](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02701)

name: Electronic side of thermoelectrics
summary: The thermoelectric figure of merit depends on the Seebeck coefficient and electrical conductivity from Boltzmann transport (Mott formula) and on the electronic thermal conductivity fixed by Wiedemann-Franz; band engineering optimizes the power factor S^2 sigma.

name: Landauer transport in nanoscale transistors
summary: As MOSFET channels shrink to a few nanometres, current is computed as transmission through modes (Landauer-Buttiker, non-equilibrium Green's functions) rather than drift-diffusion; the ballistic limit gives the conductance quantum per mode.
sources: Datta (2004). "Quantum Transport: Atom to Transistor". *Cambridge University Press*. [doi:10.1017/cbo9781139164313.012](https://doi.org/10.1017/cbo9781139164313.012)

name: Phonon engineering for thermoelectrics
summary: High ZT needs low lattice thermal conductivity: strong anharmonicity, Umklapp and boundary scattering of phonons (as in SnSe and nanostructured bulk) suppress kappa_L without hurting electrons.
sources: Zhao et al. (2014). "Ultralow thermal conductivity and high thermoelectric figure of merit in SnSe crystals". *Nature* 508, 373. [doi:10.1038/nature13184](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature13184)

name: Raman and infrared spectroscopy of phonons
summary: Molecular vibrational spectroscopy carries over to crystals, where Raman and IR probe zone-centre optical phonons; in graphene the G and 2D Raman bands count layers, measure strain, doping and electron-phonon coupling.
sources: Ferrari et al. (2006). "Raman Spectrum of Graphene and Graphene Layers". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 97, 187401. [arXiv:cond-mat/0606284](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0606284)

name: Polaron hopping and Marcus electron transfer
summary: Small-polaron hopping in solids (Holstein) and Marcus electron transfer in solution are the same theory: an electron moves between sites when vibrational (phonon) fluctuations bring the two diabatic energies into resonance, with reorganization energy equal to twice the polaron binding energy.
sources: Holstein (1959). "Studies of polaron motion: Part II. The 'small' polaron". *Ann. Phys.* 8, 343. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(59)90003-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(59)90003-X)

name: Device physics built on semiconductor physics
summary: Applied device physics (transistors, photovoltaics, sensors, thermoelectrics) rests on semiconductor band structure, doping and carrier transport.

name: NV centres: point defects in a wide-gap semiconductor
summary: The nitrogen-vacancy centre is a deep point defect in diamond's 5.5 eV gap whose spin triplet ground state is optically initialized and read out at room temperature, making defect physics of semiconductors the basis of nanoscale quantum sensing.
map: H=DS_z^2+\gamma_e\mathbf B\cdot\mathbf S,\ D/h\approx2.87\,\text{GHz};\ \delta B\sim\frac{1}{\gamma C\sqrt{T_2t}}
sources: Doherty et al. (2013). "The nitrogen-vacancy colour centre in diamond". *Phys. Rep.* 528, 1. [arXiv:1302.3288](https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.3288)

name: Semiconductor physics and semiconductor devices
summary: Doped silicon, III-V and wide-gap semiconductors are one object seen twice: condensed matter supplies gaps, mobilities, recombination and junction physics; device physics turns them into MOSFETs, LEDs, lasers and photovoltaics.
sources: Bardeen & Brattain (1948). "The Transistor, A Semi-Conductor Triode". *Phys. Rev.* 74, 230. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.74.230](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.74.230)
Shockley & Queisser (1961). "Detailed Balance Limit of Efficiency of p-n Junction Solar Cells". *J. Appl. Phys.* 32, 510. [doi:10.1063/1.1736034](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1736034)

name: Graphene nanopores for single-molecule sensing
summary: A single graphene layer is thinner than the spacing of DNA bases, so ionic current through a graphene nanopore resolves translocating molecules with sub-nanometre thickness, a step toward solid-state sequencing.
sources: Garaj et al. (2010). "Graphene as a subnanometre trans-electrode membrane". *Nature* 467, 190. [arXiv:1006.3518](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.3518)

name: Quantum-dot light emitters and photovoltaics
summary: Size-tuned colloidal and perovskite nanocrystals are used in displays (QLEDs), downconverters and solar cells; confinement sets the emission colour and multiple-exciton generation offers a route past the Shockley-Queisser limit.
sources: Murray, Norris & Bawendi (1993). "Synthesis and characterization of nearly monodisperse CdE (E = sulfur, selenium, tellurium) semiconductor nanocrystallites". *J. Am. Chem. Soc.* 115, 8706. [doi:10.1021/ja00072a025](https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00072a025)

name: Two-dimensional semiconductor channels for transistors
summary: Monolayer MoS2 and related TMDs provide atomically thin channels with sizeable gaps, immune to short-channel effects that limit silicon scaling; contact resistance and dielectric integration are the open device problems.
sources: Radisavljevic et al. (2011). "Single-layer MoS2 transistors". *Nat. Nanotechnol.* 6, 147. [doi:10.1038/nnano.2010.279](https://doi.org/10.1038/nnano.2010.279)

name: NV magnetometry imaging of 2D magnets
summary: Scanning single-spin (NV) magnetometry images stray fields of atomically thin magnets such as CrI3 quantitatively, resolving layer-dependent magnetization and domains; it is now a standard probe of 2D magnetism and spin textures.
sources: Thiel et al. (2019). "Probing magnetism in 2D materials at the nanoscale with single-spin microscopy". *Science* 364, 973. [arXiv:1902.01406](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.01406)

name: Crackling noise: Barkhausen jumps and earthquakes
summary: Barkhausen noise from domain-wall avalanches in ferromagnets and earthquakes on faults both show power-law size distributions explained by depinning of an elastic interface in a random medium, the 'crackling noise' universality family.
breaks: Fault systems have long-range elastic interactions, healing and inertia that can produce characteristic quakes; universality-class assignments and exponents differ, and magnetic avalanches are tuned by an external field rather than tectonic loading.
sources: Sethna, Dahmen & Myers (2001). "Crackling noise". *Nature* 410, 242. [arXiv:cond-mat/0102091](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0102091)

name: Rock magnetism and the paleomagnetic record
summary: Remanent magnetization of magnetite-bearing rocks, explained by Neel's theory of thermally activated single-domain grains, records the geomagnetic field; stripes of reversed magnetization on the sea floor confirmed sea-floor spreading and plate tectonics.
sources: Vine & Matthews (1963). "Magnetic Anomalies Over Oceanic Ridges". *Nature* 199, 947. [doi:10.1038/199947a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/199947a0)

name: Spintronic memory and read heads in electronics
summary: Giant and tunnelling magnetoresistance moved from discovery to hard-disk read heads within a decade, and spin-transfer-torque MRAM is now embedded in CMOS logic processes as non-volatile memory.
sources: Baibich et al. (1988). "Giant Magnetoresistance of (001)Fe/(001)Cr Magnetic Superlattices". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 61, 2472. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2472](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2472)

name: Soft-matter physics of biological materials
summary: Membranes, biopolymers, gels and cytoskeletal networks have energies of order k_BT, so entropic elasticity, fluctuations, self-assembly and viscoelasticity, the core of soft matter, set the mechanics of cells and biomolecules.
sources: de Gennes (1992). "Soft matter". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 64, 645. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.64.645](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.64.645)

name: Cells and tissues as active matter
summary: The actomyosin cortex and epithelial tissues are active gels and active nematics; topological defects in epithelial monolayers localize stress and trigger cell extrusion, the same +1/2 defect physics as in microtubule active nematics.
sources: Marchetti et al. (2013). "Hydrodynamics of soft active matter". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 85, 1143. [arXiv:1207.2929](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.2929)
Saw et al. (2017). "Topological defects in epithelia govern cell death and extrusion". *Nature* 544, 212. [doi:10.1038/nature21718](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature21718)

name: Flocking theory and collective animal behaviour
summary: Vicsek and Toner-Tu theories of polar active matter describe starling flocks, fish schools and bacterial swarms; field data showing starlings interact with a fixed number of topological neighbours fed back into active-matter models.
sources: Vicsek et al. (1995). "Novel Type of Phase Transition in a System of Self-Driven Particles". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 75, 1226. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1226](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1226)

Ballerini et al. (2008). "Interaction ruling animal collective behavior depends on topological rather than metric distance: Evidence from a field study". *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 105, 1232. [arXiv:0709.1916](https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1916)

name: Brownian colloids as force probes
summary: Optical and magnetic tweezers are calibrated by the Brownian motion of a trapped colloidal bead: equipartition and the Lorentzian power spectrum with Stokes drag give the trap stiffness that turns position into force.

name: Granular friction and earthquake faults
summary: Fault gouge is a sheared granular layer: rate-and-state friction, stick-slip instability, dilatancy and shear localization measured on granular materials explain earthquake nucleation and aftershock behaviour.
sources: Marone (1998). "Laboratory-derived friction laws and their application to seismic faulting". *Annu. Rev. Earth Planet. Sci.* 26, 643. [doi:10.1146/annurev.earth.26.1.643](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.earth.26.1.643)

name: Phase-change glasses for non-volatile memory
summary: Chalcogenide glasses such as Ge2Sb2Te5 switch in nanoseconds between amorphous and crystalline states with very different resistivity and reflectivity; crystallization kinetics and glass stability are the device physics of phase-change memory.
sources: Wuttig & Yamada (2007). "Phase-change materials for rewriteable data storage". *Nat. Mater.* 6, 824. [doi:10.1038/nmat2009](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmat2009)

name: Jamming and unjamming of biological tissues
summary: Confluent epithelia undergo a rigidity (jamming) transition controlled by cell shape rather than density, analogous to athermal jamming; unjammed, fluid-like tissue is linked to wound healing, asthma and cancer invasion.
sources: Bi et al. (2015). "A density-independent rigidity transition in biological tissues". *Nat. Phys.* 11, 1074. [arXiv:1409.0593](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0593)

name: Rugged energy landscapes: glasses and protein folding
summary: Random-energy and spin-glass landscape ideas developed for glass formers were applied to proteins, giving the folding funnel and the principle of minimal frustration: foldable sequences have a folding temperature well above their glass temperature.
sources: Bryngelson & Wolynes (1987). "Spin glasses and the statistical mechanics of protein folding". *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 84, 7524. [doi:10.1073/pnas.84.21.7524](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.84.21.7524)

name: Helfrich elasticity: from liquid crystals to membranes
summary: Lipid bilayers are two-dimensional smectic-A liquid crystals; Helfrich, co-inventor of the twisted-nematic display, transferred Frank curvature elasticity to membranes, giving the bending energy that predicts red-blood-cell shapes and vesicle fluctuations.
sources: Helfrich (1973). "Elastic Properties of Lipid Bilayers: Theory and Possible Experiments". *Z. Naturforsch. C* 28, 693. [doi:10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209](https://doi.org/10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209)

name: Proteins and nucleic acids as polymers
summary: Polymer physics (random walks, excluded volume, theta collapse, persistence length) gives the baseline for unfolded proteins and DNA; folding is a heteropolymer collapse with sequence-specific interactions.
sources: Flory (1949). "The Configuration of Real Polymer Chains". *J. Chem. Phys.* 17, 303. [doi:10.1063/1.1747243](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1747243)

name: Flory-Huggins phase separation and biomolecular condensates
summary: Membraneless organelles (P granules, nucleoli, stress granules) form by liquid-liquid phase separation of multivalent proteins and RNA, described with Flory-Huggins polymer-solution theory and its sticker-spacer extensions.
sources: Brangwynne et al. (2009). "Germline P Granules Are Liquid Droplets That Localize by Controlled Dissolution/Condensation". *Science* 324, 1729. [doi:10.1126/science.1172046](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1172046)

Hyman, Weber & Jülicher (2014). "Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation in Biology". *Annu. Rev. Cell Dev. Biol.* 30, 39. [doi:10.1146/annurev-cellbio-100913-013325](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-cellbio-100913-013325)

name: Worm-like chain elasticity of single DNA molecules
summary: Force-extension curves of single DNA molecules in optical and magnetic tweezers are fitted by the worm-like-chain model of semiflexible polymers, giving a 50 nm persistence length and confirming entropic elasticity at the single-molecule level.
sources: Bustamante et al. (1994). "Entropic elasticity of λ-phage DNA". *Science* 265, 1599. [doi:10.1126/science.8079175](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.8079175)

name: DMRG, QMC and coupled cluster across fields
summary: DMRG, invented for 1D spin chains, became a leading method for strongly correlated molecules (active spaces of transition-metal clusters), while coupled cluster and quantum Monte Carlo moved from nuclear and quantum chemistry into solids; agreement across methods is the benchmark standard in both fields.
sources: Chan & Sharma (2011). "The Density Matrix Renormalization Group in Quantum Chemistry". *Annu. Rev. Phys. Chem.* 62, 465. [doi:10.1146/annurev-physchem-032210-103338](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-physchem-032210-103338)

name: Superconductors in accelerators
summary: Accelerators are the largest users of applied superconductivity: NbTi and Nb3Sn dipoles and quadrupoles bend and focus beams, and superconducting niobium RF cavities provide high-gradient, low-loss acceleration.

name: BCS surface resistance of SRF cavities
summary: Niobium superconducting RF cavities are limited by the BCS surface resistance from thermally excited quasiparticles, plus residual losses from trapped flux; nitrogen doping and Nb3Sn coatings are gap-engineering responses that raise Q0 and gradient.

name: Superconducting magnets for MRI
summary: Clinical MRI scanners use persistent-mode NbTi solenoids at 1.5-7 T; type-II superconductivity with strong flux pinning gives the stable, homogeneous field whose Larmor frequency sets image signal and resolution.

name: Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering of cuprates
summary: High-resolution RIXS at synchrotrons measures paramagnons and charge-density-wave correlations in cuprates; it revealed incommensurate charge order competing with superconductivity in YBCO.
sources: Ghiringhelli et al. (2012). "Long-Range Incommensurate Charge Fluctuations in (Y,Nd)Ba2Cu3O6+x". *Science* 337, 821. [arXiv:1207.0915](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.0915)

name: SQUID magnetometry
summary: SQUIDs turn flux quantization and Josephson interference into femtotesla magnetometers used for magnetoencephalography, geophysics, rock magnetism and condensed-matter susceptibility measurements.
sources: Hämäläinen et al. (1993). "Magnetoencephalography—theory, instrumentation, and applications to noninvasive studies of the working human brain". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 65, 413. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.65.413](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.65.413)

name: Topological origin of equatorial waves
summary: Applying Chern-number band topology to the rotating shallow-water equations shows that the equatorial Kelvin and Yanai waves are topologically protected edge modes forced by the sign change of the Coriolis parameter at the equator.
sources: Delplace, Marston & Venaille (2017). "Topological origin of equatorial waves". *Science* 358, 1075. [arXiv:1702.07583](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.07583)

name: Synchrotron ARPES of topological surface states
summary: Spin- and angle-resolved photoemission with tunable synchrotron light identified the odd number of spin-momentum-locked surface Dirac cones that define 3D topological insulators, and later Fermi arcs in Weyl semimetals.
sources: Hsieh et al. (2008). "A topological Dirac insulator in a quantum spin Hall phase". *Nature* 452, 970. [arXiv:0902.1356](https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.1356)
